correctness.rationale: All real depths and positive thresholds are covered by the strict-chamber Jacobian reduction; every binary Haar active-set projector is locally realizable. Open-path variation decomposes exactly into unit steps and only one Haar detail per dyadic scale has nonzero projection against a given jump. Direct orthonormal inner products give the signed rational step-response vectors, hence the exact finite formula and attainment. Each response has variation ≤2, yielding 2d. At cut (2^d−1)/3 for even d, scales 2 mod 4 have disjoint derivative supports and variation ≥1 each; duplication extends the lower bound to odd d. The embedded integer-only checker exhausts all cuts and relevant masks for d≤8 and verifies the lower-bound witnesses at d=4,8,12,16. Finite checks supplement the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Soft Haar thresholding is an important canonical nonlinear transform; L2 nonexpansivity and one-input variation diminution do not measure two-input BV sensitivity. The exact, attained low-depth threshold constants and practical all-depth reduction provide useful resolution-dependent stability benchmarks. The proof exhibits a structural nonlocal multiscale mechanism forcing logarithmically unbounded pairwise variation amplification, unlike a narrow arbitrary finite computation.
